thread: tara-docs: starting a tiny PR to add an Ubuntu 22.04 systemd socket-activation example for the HSM agent on private installs. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/2007 jon-engr: nice. socket activation helps reduce idle memory on small edge nodes. can you show both systemd unit + socket files and a note about `ProtectSystem` so we don't allow accidental write access to /usr. tara-docs: will do. plan: two files `redwood-hsm.socket` and `redwood-hsm@.service`, plus a short line about drop-in settings for constrained devices. snippet: ```ini # redwood-hsm.socket [Unit] Description=Redwood HSM socket [Socket] ListenStream=/var/run/redwood/hsm.sock SocketMode=0660 SocketUser=redwood SocketGroup=redwood [Install] WantedBy=sockets.target ``` ```ini # redwood-hsm@.service [Unit] Description=Redwood HSM agent for %i After=network.target [Service] ExecStart=/usr/bin/redwood-hsm --config /etc/redwood/hsm/%i.conf User=redwood Group=redwood ProtectSystem=full ProtectHome=yes NoNewPrivileges=yes PrivateTmp=yes RuntimeDirectory=redwood RuntimeDirectoryMode=0750 [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target ``` paul-qa: couple test notes: 1) ensure the socket dir exists with correct SELinux label on RHEL, 2) on Ubuntu check `systemd-socket-proxyd` won't steal the socket when you restart. add a troubleshooting bullet for `Address already in use` -> leftover socket file -> `systemctl daemon-reload && rm /var/run/redwood/hsm.sock` and restart. jon-engr: also include a short Go SDK snippet showing how clients should connect over unix socket for embeddings requests in private deploys: ```go // dial unix socket conn, err := net.Dial("unix", "/var/run/redwood/hsm.sock") if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } client := NewRedwoodClient(conn) // use client... ``` tara-docs: good. will add under "SDK examples" and mention file permissions and capability requirements. ops-bot: CI
